LESSON: CLOTHING CONSTRUCTION PROCESSES ● STITCHES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: HOME SCIENCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Clothing and Textiles
Topic 3.4: Clothing Construction Processes ● Stitches
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Clothing Construction Processes ● Stitches, part of Clothing and Textiles in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 HOME SCIENCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How do different stitches affect the quality and durability of a garment? 2. How can stitches be creatively used in clothing construction?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Clothing Construction Processes ● Stitches together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: the learner clearly describes the procedure followed when working the stitches and gives focused feedback

during class presentations.

● Communication and Collaboration: the learners participate actively in working out stitches and peer assess each other’s

work.

● Digital Literacy: the learners access information from digital learning platforms on procedures of working out different

stitches.

40

Values:
● Unity: learners appreciate the efforts of others when making different stitches.

● Respect: the learners appreciate diverse opinions during discussions on different types of stitches.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Socio-economic and Environmental issues: Learners tactfully manage waste accrued from the clippings and chippings of

the fabrics and threads.

● Safety in the Laboratory: as learners practise safety measures in the Home Science workshop.
